record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Characterize the compact spaces K for which the Banach space C(K) has the following property: whenever C(K) is a subspace of a Banach space Z and the quotient Z/C(K) is isomorphic to C(K), the subspace C(K) is complemented in Z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a compact Hausdorff space $K$, let $C(K)$ denote the Banach space of continuous real-valued (or complex-valued) functions on $K$ endowed with the supremum norm. Say that a Banach space $X$ has the self-extension splitting property if, for every Banach space $Z$ that contains a closed subspace isomorphic to $X$ such that the quotient $Z/X$ is isomorphic to $X$, this subspace is complemented in $Z$ (equivalently, every short exact sequence $0 \to X \to Z \to X \to 0$ of Banach spaces splits).

Characterize the compact Hausdorff spaces $K$ for which $C(K)$ has the self-extension splitting property.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed in a 2014 collection of open problems in Banach space theory and is listed there as an open problem. Related work studies nontrivial twisted sums of $c_0$ or $C(K)$ with $C(K)$, but a full characterization of compacta $K$ for which $C(K)$ has the stated self-extension splitting property does not appear to be available. No published solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
status_evidence.snippet: Problems where if X is a subspace of Z such that Z/X is isomorphic to X, then X is complemented in Z, and the problem of characterizing such spaces among C(K).
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in this 2014 problem collection.

status_evidence.title: Extension operators and twisted sums of c0 and C(K) spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Nontrivial twisted sums of c0 and C(K): a Banach space X containing a non-complemented copy of c0 with quotient isomorphic to C(K).
status_evidence.claim: Related results on twisted sums with C(K) but no characterization of the self-extension splitting property for general C(K).
